Load and Normalize Nanostring gene expression data

Source: R/loadnormalizercc.R
loadnormalizercc.Rd

loadnormalizercc is used to read the raw nSolver data saved in RCC file and normalize the data using nSolver or RUVg method.

Usage

loadnormalizercc(
  dir,
  meta_dir,
  file_number = TRUE,
  normalization = "none",
  bd_low = 0.05,
  bd_high = 2.25,
  numSD = 0,
  hkgenes = "",
  exclude = NULL,
  k,
  rlf = NULL,
  phenoDataRccColName = ""
)

Arguments

dir

Path to the NanoString files (make sure the folder contains only the files with .RCC extension).

meta_dir

Path to the meta data file (Consider meta_GSE146530.csv as a template).

file_number

TRUE or FALSE. When TRUE, numbers will be printed when the RCC files are accessed.

normalization

Anyone of the following should be provided: "none" or "nSolver" or "RUVg". Default is "none".

bd_low

The lower limit for binding density (QC Flag). Default is 0.05.

bd_high

The upper limit for binding density (QC Flag). Default is 2.25.

numSD

The number of standard deviations to calibrate the LOD (QC Flag). Default is 0.

hkgenes

A vector of HouseKeeping gene names.

exclude

A vector of HouseKeeping gene to exclude (applicable only to RUVg normalization).

k

The number of dimensions of unwanted variation estimated (applicable only to RUVg normalization).

rlf

Path to the respective RLF file (applicable only to nsolver normalization).

phenoDataRccColName

Column name in meta data that specifies the RCC files (applicable only to nSolver normalization).

Value

A list of variables containing (not limited to) either a matrix of raw expression values of genes or a matrix of log2 transformed normalized genes, phenotype data (pdata), feature data (fdata), expression sets and number of endogenous genes in the samples that are below the Limit Of Detection (LOD).

Details

This function considers the directory of RCC files and meta data. In the meta data file, the first column is assumed to contain the RCC file names and the subsequent columns are the sample characteristics. Any rows with duplicated entries will be dropped and the first one will be retained.

Author

Jayanth Sreekanth

Examples


path_to_rcc <- system.file("extdata", "GSE146530", package = "rhythmCI")
meta <- system.file("extdata", "meta_GSE146530.csv", package = "rhythmCI")

# Load and No normalization -----------------------------------------------------------------

exp_df1 <- loadnormalizercc(dir = path_to_rcc, meta_dir = meta,
  hkgenes = c("LOC106606270", "LOC106600007"), file_number = FALSE)

df1_raw <- exp_df1$rawdata
df1_pdata <- exp_df1$pData
df1_fdata <- exp_df1$fData
df1_endblod <- exp_df1$num_endogenous_blod
df1_lodmatrix <- exp_df1$lod_matrix

# Genes in the samples that are below the Limit Of Detection (LOD) has TRUE value
# in the matrix "df1_lodmatrix". They need to be filtered using any of your
# preferred choice. After which, the data can be RUVg normalized
# using the function 'normalizeruvg'. nSolver normalization is not available in this case.

# Load and perform nSolver normalization ----------------------------------------------------
suppressWarnings(

exp_df2 <- loadnormalizercc(dir = path_to_rcc, meta_dir = meta,
  normalization = "nSolver",
  hkgenes = c("LOC106606270", "LOC106600007"), phenoDataRccColName = 'files.RCC',
  file_number = FALSE)
)

df2_nsolverexpset <- exp_df2$nsolverexpset
df2_nsolvernormlog2 <- exp_df2$nsolvernormlog2
df2_pdata <- exp_df2$pData
df2_fdata <- exp_df2$fData
df2_endblod <- exp_df2$num_endogenous_blod

# Load and perform RUVg normalization -------------------------------------------------------
suppressMessages(

exp_df3 <- loadnormalizercc(dir = path_to_rcc, meta_dir = meta,
  normalization = "RUVg",
  hkgenes = c("LOC106606270", "LOC106600007"), k=3,
  file_number = FALSE)
)

df3_set <- exp_df3$set
df3_vsd <- exp_df3$vsd
df3_ruvgnormlog2 <- exp_df3$ruvgnormlog2
df3_pdata <- exp_df3$pData
df3_fdata <- exp_df3$fData
df3_endblod <- exp_df3$num_endogenous_blod
